framing: Test the model, then test the test
paragraphs: Before replacing a model, verify that candidate outputs improve on the requests your application actually handles. Public leaderboards show which weights merit consideration, while private evaluation suites confirm whether the complete request path preserves critical specifications or invents unsafe shortcuts.

Automated scorers fail in surprising ways too. A mandatory keyword can appear inside an answer that negates the rule, while an accurate paraphrase misses exact-string patterns completely, and an LLM judge can favor whichever completion occupies the first slot. Treating every scorer as software with its own challenge suite prevents bad metrics from approving unsafe systems.

Fair comparisons also isolate one variable at a time. Recording dataset splits, retrieved passages, prompt templates, chat serialization, decoding settings, scorer versions, and holdout usage ensures a genuine weight improvement stands cleanly apart from retrieval or harness edits.

Together, these checks yield a release decision any teammate can verify: targeted tasks aligned with real risks, failure breakdowns across critical slices, honest Wilson uncertainty intervals on small samples, and latency and cost budgets measured alongside quality.
outcomes: Author private evaluation suites and stress-test scorers with negations and paraphrases.
Separate retrieval coverage misses from generation errors and enforce order-swapped judge checks.
Compare models via paired McNemar tests and evaluate failure slices, confidence intervals, latency, and cost together.
question: Which parts of an evaluation claim must be rerun if an apparent model gain also widened retrieval depth and tuned its automated judge on reported holdout cases?
